"It guides to righteousness (rushd)": That is, to what is correct in belief, speech and action.

"And exalted is the majesty (jadd) of our Lord": That is, the majesty and greatness of our Lord is exalted above what is attributed to Him.

"He has taken neither a consort nor a son": That is, He has not taken a consort, nor has He had a son.

"Our foolish one (safihuna)": That is, our ignorant one.

"Outrageous (shatatan)": That is, excess in lying by describing God, exalted is He, with a consort and a son.

"Lies about God": Until it became clear to us that they lie about God by ascribing a wife and a son to Him.

"Seek refuge (ya'udhun)": That is, they seek refuge.

"So they increased them in burden (rahqan)": That is, in sin and transgression.

"That God would never raise up anyone": That is, He would never send a messenger to His creation.

The Most High's words, ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened"﴾: The Most High commands His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to say, announcing it to people, believers and disbelievers alike, that God the Most High has revealed to him a report that a group of the jinn, between three and ten of them, listened to his recitation of the Qur'an. This took place in the valley of Nakhla, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. The Messenger (ﷺ) was, at that time, heading with his companions to the market of 'Ukaz. On that day, the devils had been barred from the heavens and from eavesdropping, for meteors had been hurled at them. So the devils consulted one another and concluded that something momentous had happened. They set off traveling through the eastern and western regions of the earth, seeking to learn about this great event due to which the devils had been prevented from the heavens. A group of them headed toward Tihama and found the Messenger (ﷺ) praying the dawn prayer with his companions, so they listened to his recitation in his prayer. They returned to their people among the jinn and said, ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to righteousness, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾. In this there is a rebuke to the foolishness of the humans among whom the Messenger lived for eleven years, reciting the Qur'an to them in Mecca while they denied it, hated it, and persisted in polytheism, whereas the jinn, as soon as they heard it, believed in it and carried its message to their people. And here they are, spreading the call of Islam, saying, ﴿So we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. And exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾, meaning: and we believe that He, the Most High, is exalted in majesty, our Lord and Sovereign, ﴿He has taken neither a consort nor a son﴾, and far is He from that; rather, such things were attributed to Him by the fabricators.

﴿And that our foolish one used to say outrageous things about God﴾: This is from the speech of the jinn, who continued their account saying: "And that our ignorant one used to speak outrageous lies about God," meaning, excess in lying by describing God the Most High with a consort and a son, imitating the polytheists, the Jews and the Christians. ﴿And we had thought that humans and jinn would never speak a lie about God﴾: That is, they told their people, "We used to think that humans and jinn would not lie about God, and would say nothing about Him but the truth. Now we know that they lie about God and say of Him what He has not said, and attribute to Him what is free of Him." They also said, ﴿And that there were men of humankind who sought refuge with men of the jinn, so they increased them in burden﴾: They related a strange report, namely that men of humankind, from among the Arabs and others, when they stopped at a frightening place in a valley or a ravine, would seek refuge with men of the jinn, as a man would say, "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people." Thus humans increased the jinn in rahaq (burden) by this seeking of their protection and taking refuge in them, that is, in sin and transgression. For the jinn had not expected that humans would glorify them to such a degree as to seek their protection. ﴿And they thought, as you thought, that God would never raise up anyone﴾: That is, they told their people that humans thought, just as you, O jinn, thought, that God would never send a messenger to warn people of God's punishment and to teach them what perfects them and brings them happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

1. Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood, and that Muhammad is a messenger to both humankind and jinn together.
2. Demonstration of the exalted status and perfection of the Qur'an, for the jinn testified that it is wondrous, beyond the level of created speech.
3. Affirmation of monotheism and condemnation of polytheism.
4. Affirmation that humans, like the jinn, may lie about God, though that was never permissible for them.
5. The prohibition of seeking help from the jinn and seeking refuge with them, since that is like worshipping them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 72, verses 25–28:

Explanation of the words:

"Qul in adri" (Say: I do not know): that is, say: I do not know.

"Ma tu'adun" (what you are promised): that is, of the punishment.

"Amadan" (a term): that is, a limit and an appointed time which no one knows but Him.

"Fala yuzhiru" (He does not reveal): that is, He does not disclose.

"Man irtada min rasul" (any messenger whom He has approved): that is, then He informs him.

"Rasadan" (a guard): that is, angels who protect it until it reaches him, along with the revelation that he conveys to all of mankind.

"Liya'lam" (that He may know): that is, Allah knows with the knowledge of manifestation that the messengers have conveyed the messages of their Lord.

"Ahsa kulla shay'in 'adadan" (He has enumerated everything in number): that is, He has counted the number of everything.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Say: I do not know﴾. Allah commands His Messenger to say to the polytheists, who demand the punishment mockingly, obstinately and in denial, that he should tell them: I do not know whether what your Lord has promised you of punishment is near, so that it will descend upon you quickly, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term, a distant limit known to Him alone and unknown to anyone else. He is the Knower of the unseen, for He alone is the Knower of the unseen, and so He does not reveal His unseen to anyone of His servants, that is, He does not inform anyone of His unseen, except whichever messenger He approves, that is, whom He chooses to convey on His behalf. Then He informs him, with sufficient precaution so that the unseen news does not leak out to people. ﴿For He sends before him and behind him guards﴾: the approved messenger has, before and behind him, guards from the angels. Then He informs him within the revelation that is revealed to him. This is so that the Messenger ﷺ may know that the messengers before him had conveyed the messages of their Lord, because Allah, the Exalted, surrounded them with His care. Indeed, when revelation came to him, four angels were with him to protect him from the devils, so that they would not hear news from the heavens and convey it to their allies among mankind, thereby causing turmoil among the people. And His saying ﴿and He encompasses what is with them﴾: that is, Allah, majestic in His majesty, encompasses by His knowledge what is with the angels and the messengers. ﴿And He has enumerated everything in number﴾: that is, He has counted the number of everything, so nothing is hidden from Him in the earth or in the heavens, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah's exclusive possession of the knowledge of the unseen; none knows the unseen except Allah.

2- Allah may inform whichever messenger He approves of a particular portion of the unseen, and this is done after complete protection from the devils, lest they convey it to their allies and thereby cause people to be tested.
